title: Taxes
text:
The Monarch can levy taxes on trade and may raise them over time. Refusing an increase can lead to a boycott: the affected goods can no longer be bought or sold in Europe under those rules.

A boycott may be ended by paying tax arrears or through another remedy defined by the rules. Tax rates and consequences depend on the active ruleset.

title: Efficiency
text:
A colony's political mood affects its production. Support for independence can grant production bonuses, while a large royalist population can reduce production. The exact thresholds depend on difficulty and the active ruleset; the current rules are listed in the facts below.

Liberty bells change political support according to the rules, and colony population also affects efficiency.

title: Education
text:
Schools let experienced colonists teach others. Which unit types can be trained and how long training takes depend on the active rules and the available school.

Skills can also be learned through work or in Indigenous settlements. Requirements, experience and possible promotions vary by unit and ruleset.

title: Fortification
text: Units can use the fortify order to secure their position. Its duration, protection and combat bonuses depend on the unit, terrain and active ruleset. Other defensive features of a tile or colony may change the additional benefit.

title: Independence
text:
One possible goal is to make the colonies independent from the home country. Liberty bells and the population's political support play a part; the active rules define the required conditions.

A declaration of independence can trigger a war with the Royal Expeditionary Force. Victory conditions, army strength and defeat conditions depend on the game rules.

title: Royal Expeditionary Force
text:
In classic rules, the Monarch can send a Royal Expeditionary Force (REF) to oppose a declaration of independence. Its composition and reinforcements depend on the game and active rules.

The unit entries show the current attributes of forces in the ruleset.

title: Intervention Force
text: Some classic rules include an Intervention Force that can support the rebels during the War of Independence. Whether it appears, when it arrives and which units it contains depend on the rules and the course of the game.

title: Developing Colonies
text:
A colony connects its center, surrounding tiles and buildings into an economy. Assign colonists to suitable workplaces and compare building inputs and outputs with the terrain and goods facts.

Food, available workers, storage and building materials all affect development. The active rules determine yields and requirements.

title: Production Chains
text:
Many goods are produced in stages: raw materials are gathered and refined in appropriate buildings. Each production site can consume some goods and create others.

Check a building's inputs, outputs and modifiers, as well as workers' equipment and skills. Displayed amounts come from the active specification.

title: Trade and the Market
text:
Goods can move between colonies, Europe and other trading partners. Market prices respond to supply and demand; imports, exports, taxes and boycotts can affect trade.

Goods facts show the reference price and quantity from the rules. The current price may change with the actual market stock.

title: Exploration
text:
Exploring units reveal unknown areas and can discover terrain, resources and settlements. Movement, sight and special abilities vary by unit.

Use the unit and resource facts to choose an exploration team. Encounters with settlements may lead to trade, knowledge or political consequences.

title: Relations with Indigenous Peoples
text:
Indigenous settlements are independent actors. Encounters may allow trade, knowledge exchange, missionary work or conflict; available actions depend on the unit, relationship and ruleset.

Review the entries for the units, roles and nations involved before approaching a settlement.
